correctness.rationale: For every 2<=p<=q, rank(L)=N-1 and group permutations force the unique minimum ball center into a one-dimensional invariant subspace. Two explicitly computed convex quadratics govern the full vertex set; their crossing and critical points give the stated min(a0,q/p). Both squared-radius branches and contact clearance follow by algebra. The resulting center is a convex combination of its touching vertices, which independently certifies global minimality. The extracted script passed 138 reconstructed cases (77 screening); finite checks are corroborative, not substitutes for the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2017 original Laplacian-simplex paper establishes the construction and lattice/Ehrhart properties but no Euclidean minimum-sphere result; the 2018 continuation addresses code and lattice invariants. A published vertex-transitive Laplacian-simplex theorem gives the p=q balanced special case, not the p<q screening threshold; its full RESULT statement was compared. A second published tree theorem treats inradius and thus neither implies this outer-sphere classification nor covers p>=2. The non-Euclidean Laplacian-lattice paper does not measure canonical Euclidean vertex circumballs. No covering implication was identified, with historical-priority risk retained for differently named simplex-center results.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the complete Euclidean minimum-enclosing-ball contact classification of a natural two-parameter graph-simplex family, revealing a sharp transition from all N vertices to exactly p vertices on the optimal sphere and an explicit strict clearance of each screened vertex. In the adjacent K(3,13) and K(3,14) cases the number of contact vertices drops from 16 to 3. This discriminates the classical all-vertex equidistant sphere from the genuinely minimal enclosing sphere in a way not captured by simplex face structure or lattice invariants.
